RED | logo = | website = {{URL|https://www.buet.ac.bd/}} }} '''Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology''', commonly known by the [[acronym]] '''BUET,''' is a [[public university|public]] [[Institute of technology|technological research university]] in [[Dhaka]], [[Bangladesh]]. Founded in 1876 as the '''Dacca Survey School''', it is the oldest institution for the study of [[engineering]], [[architecture]], and [[urban planning]] in Bangladesh.{{Cite news |script-title=bn:বাংলাদেশ প্রকৌশল বিশ্ববিদ্যালয় (বুয়েট)|url=https://www.kalerkantho.com/feature/tuntuntintin/2012/08/10/276902|access-date=8 April 2021|work=Kaler Kantho|date=10 August 2012 |language=bn}} A large number of [[List of Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology alumni|BUET alumni]] are active in notable engineering and non-engineering roles in Bangladesh and abroad.{{Cite web|title=Talented graduates prefer to study abroad|url=https://bangladeshpost.net/posts/talented-graduates-prefer-to-study-abroad-10887|access-date=6 June 2021|website=bangladeshpost.net|language=en}}{{Cite news |script-title=bn:বুয়েটের সাফল্য বিশ্বব্যাপী, প্রাপ্তি অনেক|url=https://www.banglanews24.com/banglanews-special/news/bd/35812.details|access-date=8 April 2021|work=banglanews24.com|date=10 April 2011 |language=bn}} [[File:বুয়েট এলাকা (BUET Area).jpg|alt=BUET area.|left|thumb|BUET area.]] ==History== {{multiple image | align = left | image1 = Salimullah.jpg | caption1 = Nawab Bahadur Sir [[Khwaja Salimullah]] released a grant in 1902 in accordance with the wish of his late father and as an acknowledgement of this contribution, the survey school was renamed to Ahsanullah School of Engineering in 1908. | width1 = 150 }} Dacca Survey School was established in 1876 at Nalgola, west of the current [[Sir Salimullah Medical College]] campus, in [[Old Dhaka]] by the Government of [[Bengal Presidency|Bengal]] under [[British Raj]].{{cite web |url=http://en.banglapedia.org/index.php?title=Bangladesh_University_of_Engineering_and_Technology|title=Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology|access-date=8 December 2012|publisher=[[Banglapedia]], National Encyclopaedia of Bangladesh}} It offered two-year engineering and survey courses toward the Sub-Overseer's examination, which certified [[Surveying|land surveyors]].{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=cu9EAQAAMAAJ&q=%22Dacca%20Survey%20School%22&pg=PA263|title=Progress of Education in India: Quinquennial Review, Issue 4, Volumes 1-2|publisher=H.M. Stationery Office|year=1904|page=263}} According to a report on public instruction in Bengal, on 31 March 1903, Dhaka Survey School had 117 students of which 103 were Hindus and 14 were Muslims.{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=MTs_AQAAMAAJ&q=%22Dacca+Survey+School%22&pg=PA31|title=Report on Public Instruction in Bengal|publisher=Bengal (India). Education Department|year=1904|page=31}} In 1908, the school started to offer diploma degrees.{{cite news |url=http://archive.thedailystar.net/campus/2008/01/01/camspotlight.htm|title=BUET: 60 Years of Engineering Education|work=The Daily Star|date=6 January 2008|access-date=5 July 2016|author=Khan, Kamrul Hasan}} Nawab Sir [[Khwaja Ahsanullah]] Bahadur, a philanthropist and [[Nawab of Dhaka]], endowed donations for developing the survey school. After his death in 1901, his son, the then Nawab of Dhaka, Sir [[Khwaja Salimullah]] Bahadur released the grant in 1902 in accordance with his late fathers wish.{{cite book |last=Islam|first=Sirajul|year=2012|chapter=Ahsanullah, Khwaja|chapter-url=http://en.banglapedia.org/index.php?title=Ahsanullah,_Khwaja|editor1-last=Islam|editor1-first=Sirajul|editor1-link=Sirajul Islam|editor2-last=Alamgir|editor2-first=Mohammad|title=Banglapedia: National Encyclopedia of Bangladesh|edition=Second|publisher=[[Asiatic Society of Bangladesh]]}} As an acknowledgement of this contribution, the school was renamed to '''Ahsanullah School of Engineering''' in 1908. The school offered three-year [[diploma in Engineering|diploma]] courses in [[civil engineering]], [[electrical engineering]] and [[mechanical engineering]] in 1908. In 1912, the university was moved to its present premises.{{cite web |title=About BUET|url=https://www.buet.ac.bd/info/Home/About|url-status=live|access-date=15 September 2016|website=BUET|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210420175406/https://www.buet.ac.bd/info/Home/About|archive-date=20 April 2021}} In 1938, [[AK Fazlul Huq|A. K. Fazlul Huq]], the then [[Prime Minister of Bengal]], appointed Hakim Ali as the principal of the school. After the [[partition of India]] in 1947, Chief Minister of East Bengal Sir [[Khawaja Nazimuddin|Khwaja Nazimuddin]] approved the school to be upgraded to '''Ahsanullah Engineering College''', as a Faculty of Engineering under the [[University of Dhaka]], offering four-year [[bachelor's degree|bachelor's]] course in civil, electrical, mechanical, [[Chemical engineering|chemical]] and [[Metallurgy|metallurgical engineering]]. In 1948, the [[East Bengal#Nazimuddin ministry|Government of East Bengal]] granted recognition to the engineering college. Ali became the first principal of the college. In 1951, TH Mathewman was appointed the next principal. [[M. A. Rashid]] succeeded him in 1954 as the first Bengali principal of the college{{cite book |last=Islam|first=Sirajul|year=2012|chapter=Rashid, MA|chapter-url=http://en.banglapedia.org/index.php?title=Rashid,_MA|editor1-last=Islam|editor1-first=Sirajul|editor1-link=Sirajul Islam|editor2-last=Haq|editor2-first=Enamul|title=Banglapedia: National Encyclopedia of Bangladesh|edition=Second|publisher=[[Asiatic Society of Bangladesh]]}} and held the post until 1960.{{cite web |url=http://www.buet.ac.bd/rashidhall/about_dr_m_a_rashid.html|title=Dr. M. A. Rashid: A Short Biography|website=BUET|access-date=5 July 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304192815/http://www.buet.ac.bd/rashidhall/about_dr_m_a_rashid.html|archive-date=4 March 2016|url-status=dead}} In 1956, a new course curriculum and the [[Academic term|semester]] system were introduced at the college. On 1 June 1962, in order to create facilities for postgraduate studies and research, the college was upgraded to '''East Pakistan University of Engineering and Technology''' (EPUET), becoming the fourth university of the then [[East Pakistan]]. Rashid was appointed the first vice-chancellor of the university. A partnership with the Agricultural and Mechanical College of Texas (renamed [[Texas A&M University]]) was forged, and professors from A&M came to teach and formulate the curriculum. During this period, EPUET offered courses in mechanical, electrical, civil, metallurgical, and chemical engineering, and architecture. After the [[Bangladesh Liberation War|liberation war]] of 1971, and Bangladesh's independence, EPUET was renamed to '''Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology''' (BUET). In 2002, a first year student in the chemical engineering department, Sony, was killed during a factional clash between two feuding groups of the [[Bangladesh Jatiotabadi Chatra Dal|Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD)]] at BUET. The two factions exchanged gunfire and she was caught in the line of fire.{{cite news |title=Sony's death anniversary observed|url=https://bdnews24.com/politics/2005/06/07/sony-s-death-anniversary-observed|work=bdnews24.com|date=7 June 2005|access-date=21 April 2020}} In 2007, BUET celebrated 60 years (1947–2007) of engineering education in Bangladesh by arranging a 6-month-long series of programs and events.{{cite news|title=BUET starts celebrating 60 yrs of engineering education|url=http://www.thefinancialexpress-bd.com/old/2007/07/29/6063.html|access-date=8 July 2015|work=[[The Financial Express (Bangladesh)|The Financial Express]]|date=29 July 2007}} In October 2019, sophomore [[Murder of Abrar Fahad|Abrar Fahad]] was tortured and beaten to death in Sher-e-Bangla Hall, allegedly by members of the [[Bangladesh Chhatra League]] (BCL), the student wing of the ruling [[Awami League]] party.{{cite news |last1=Islam|first1=Rifat|title=Terror reigns in BUET dorms for years|url=https://www.theindependentbd.com/post/218974|work=The Independent|location=Dhaka|date=11 October 2019}}{{cite news |title=8 BUET students suspended for bullying fellows|url=https://www.newagebd.net/article/92731/8-buet-students-suspended-for-bullying-fellows|work=New Age|date=5 December 2019}} ''[[The Independent (Bangladesh)|The Independent]]'' reported that beatings and torture by the BCL were common in the dormitories. Fahad's murder sparked nearly two months of student protests against violent [[ragging]] and bullying at the residence halls.{{cite news |title=Abrar Fahad: Killing of Bangladesh student triggers protests|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/amp/world-asia-49979097|work=BBC News|access-date=21 April 2020}} The protests ended after university authorities met student demands. They expelled for life 25 students allegedly involved in the killing,{{Cite news |date=22 November 2019|title=Abrar Fahad murder: Family, protesters happy as Buet expels 25 accused|url=https://www.dhakatribune.com/bangladesh/2019/11/22/abrar-murder-buet-permanently-expels-26-students|work=Dhaka Tribune|access-date=19 September 2020}} expelled a further 15 from their places in Ahsan Ullah Hall, Suhrawardy Hall, and Titumir Hall, handed down various suspensions and warnings, and adopted new penalties for ragging and political activities.{{cite news |title=BUET expels nine students from halls for ragging|url=https://en.prothomalo.com/bangladesh/Nine-BUET-students-expelled-from-halls-for-ragging|work=Prothom Alo|date=28 November 2019}}{{cite news |title=BUET to expel any student involved in ragging, politics|url=https://bdnews24.com/campus/2019/12/03/buet-to-expel-any-student-involved-in-ragging-politics|work=bdnews24.com|date=3 December 2019}} In February 2021, BUET and [[China|Chinese]] [[Multinational corporation|multinational]] [[technology company]] [[Huawei]] signed a [[memorandum of understanding]] (MoU) to establish the first [[Information and communications technology|ICT]] Academy in Bangladesh on BUET campus.{{Cite news |date=18 February 2021|title=Huawei and Buet to set up Bangladesh's first ICT Academy by April|url=https://www.thedailystar.net/bytes/news/huawei-and-buet-set-bangladeshs-first-ict-academy-april-2047145|access-date=8 April 2021|work=The Daily Star|language=en}} On 21 June 2021, BUET and [[Saitama University]], Japan signed second renewal of the agreement on academic exchange and the memorandum on student exchange between the two institutions. Saitama University (SU) and BUET have had a long-standing relationship for the past 20 years.{{cite web|title=Online signing ceremony for the second renewal of the agreement on academic exchange and the memorandum on student exchange between Saitama University, Japan and BUET|url=https://www.buet.ac.bd/web/#/details/59}}{{cite web|title=Online Signing Ceremony for Renewal of Academic Exchange Agreement with Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology|url=http://en.saitama-u.ac.jp/news/online-signing-ceremony-for-renewal-of-academic-exchange-agreement-with-bangladesh-university-of-engineering-and-technology/}} In January 2022, BUET was ranked 1st among Bangladeshi and 1589th among global educational institutions in the [[Webometrics Ranking of World Universities]].{{cite news |script-title=bn:দেশসেরা বুয়েট, বেসরকারিতে প্রথম নর্থ সাউথ|url=https://www.prothomalo.com/feature/shapno/%E0%A6%93%E0%A7%9F%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%AC%E0%A6%AE%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%9F%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%95%E0%A6%B8-%E0%A6%B0%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AF%E0%A6%BE-%E0%A6%99%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%95%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%82%E0%A7%9F%E0%A7%87-%E0%A6%A6%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%B6%E0%A6%B8%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%BE-%E0%A6%AC%E0%A7%81%E0%A7%9F%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%9F-%E0%A6%AC%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%B8%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%95%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%A4%E0%A7%87-%E0%A6%AA%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%A5%E0%A6%AE-%E0%A6%A8%E0%A6%B0%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%A5-%E0%A6%B8%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%89%E0%A6%A5|access-date=18 February 2022|work=Prothom Alo|language=bn}} ==Academics== === Campus === BUET has an urban campus located in the Palashi area of Dhaka. The campus houses academic and administrative buildings, residential halls for students and other amenities.{{Cite news |script-title=bn:বন্ধ পলাশীর আড্ডা |language=bn |work=Prothom Alo |url=https://www.prothomalo.com/bangladesh/বন্ধ-পলাশীর-আড্ডা |access-date=9 April 2021}} ===Faculties and departments=== Academic activities are undertaken by 18 departments under five [[Faculty (division)|faculties]].{{Cite web |script-title=bn:বুয়েট: দ্য ল্যান্ড অব লিভিং|url=https://roar.media/bangla/main/architecture/buet-the-story-of-land-of-living/|access-date=9 April 2021|website=roar.media|date=16 November 2017 |language=bn}}{{cite web |title=Departments|url=http://www.buet.ac.bd/?page_id=5|url-status=live|access-date=17 December 2015|website=BUET|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070625003330/http://www.buet.ac.bd/?page_id=5|archive-date=25 June 2007}} Twelve departments offer [[Undergraduate education|undergraduate]] courses, all of which, except the Department of Humanities, offer [[Graduate school|postgraduate]] courses as well. [[File:Civil Engineering Building of BUET seen from EME Building.JPG|right|thumb|West wing of the Civil Engineering Building]] [[File:BUET EME Building.jpg|thumb|Mechanical Engineering Building]] [[File:Department of Architecture, BUET.jpg|thumb|Entry approach of the Department of Architecture, BUET]] [[File:Dept. of Architecture.jpg|thumb|Aerial view of the plinth level of the Architecture Building]] * '''Faculty of Architecture and Planning:''' ** Department of Architecture (Arch) ** Department of Urban and Regional Planning (URP) ** Department of Humanities (Hum) * '''Faculty of Civil Engineering:''' ** Department of Civil Engineering (CE){{cite web|title=BUET Civil Engineering Department|url=https://ce.buet.ac.bd/}} ** Department of Water Resources Engineering (WRE) * '''Faculty of Electrical and Electronic Engineering:''' ** Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering (EEE) ** [[Department of CSE, BUET|Department of Computer Science and Engineering]] ([[Department of CSE, BUET|CSE]]) ** Department of Biomedical Engineering (BME) * '''Faculty of Mechanical Engineering:''' ** Department of Mechanical Engineering (ME) ** Department of Industrial and Production Engineering (IPE) ** Department of Naval Architecture and Marine Engineering (NAME) * '''Faculty of Engineering:''' ** Department of Chemical Engineering (ChE) ** Department of Materials and Metallurgical Engineering (MME) ** Department of Chemistry (Chem) ** Department of Mathematics (Math) ** Department of Physics (Phys) ** Department of Petroleum and Mineral Resources Engineering (PMRE) ** Department of Nanomaterials and Ceramic Engineering (NCE){{cite web |url=https://nce.buet.ac.bd/ |title=NCE – Nanomaterials and Ceramic Engineering |website=Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology}} ===Institutes=== At present, there are six institutes in BUET. These institutes offer postgraduate diplomas, master's and doctoral degrees.{{cite web |title=Institutes|url=http://www.buet.ac.bd/?page_id=7|url-status=live|access-date=16 December 2015|website=BUET|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070625002918/http://www.buet.ac.bd/?page_id=7|archive-date=25 June 2007}} * Institute of Water and Flood Management (IWFM) * Institute of Appropriate Technology (IAT) * Institute of Information and Communication Technology (IICT) * Accident Research Institute (ARI) * BUET-Japan Institute of Disaster Prevention and Urban Safety (BUET-JIDPUS){{cite web|title=BUET-JIDPUS|url=https://jidpus.buet.ac.bd/}} * Institute of Nuclear Power Engineering (INPE) ===Research centers=== BUET has several research centres. * Centre for Energy Studies (CES) * Centre for Environmental and Resource Management (CERM) * Biomedical Engineering Centre (BEC) * Bureau of Research, Testing & Consultation (BRTC) * International Training Network Centre (ITN) * Bangladesh Network Office for Urban Safety (BNUS) ===Directorates=== * Directorate of Advisory, Extension and Research Services (DAERS) * Directorate of Students' Welfare (DSW) * Directorate of Planning and Development (P&D) * Directorate of Continuing Education (DCE) ===Journals and research bulletins=== * Journal of Mechanical Engineering Research and Developments * Chemical Engineering Research Bulletin * Bangladesh Journal of Water Resources Research * Electrical and Electronic Engineering Research Bulletin * Protibesh (Research Journal on Architecture) ===Rankings=== |website=Top Universities |language=en}} }} BUET has been ranked 202nd among the [[List of universities in Asia|Asian universities]] in the 2022 edition of [[QS World University Rankings]].{{cite web |title=Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology |url=https://www.topuniversities.com/universities/bangladesh-university-engineering-technology |access-date=19 July 2022 |publisher=[[QS World University Rankings]]}} BUET has been ranked No. 801-1000 among all universities on QS World University Rankings 2023. Only three Bangladeshi universities have been ranked in the 2022 edition of [[Times Higher Education World University Rankings]], BUET is one of them. ===Library=== BUET central [[library]] has a collection of 142,913 items of information materials. Among the materials, 125,066 and 17,847 are books and bound periodicals respectively.{{cite web |url=http://lib.buet.ac.bd/home/?q=node/10|title=Resources|website=BUET Central Library}} Besides, 152 titles are in the current subscription list of journals. Every year, 1500 volumes are added to this library. The main reading room of the central [http://lib.buet.ac.bd/home/ library] can accommodate 200 students at a time to provide reading facilities of rare and out-of-print books, and also ready reference and prescribed textbooks. There are also departmental libraries in each of the departments and institutes and hall libraries in each of the residence halls. == Convocations == After the independence of Bangladesh and the subsequent name change, the first [[convocation#Graduation|convocation]] of the university was held in 1973.{{cite news |title=9th convocation of BUET on Tuesday|work=bdnews24.com|url=http://bdnews24.com/bangladesh/2005/12/31/9th-convocation-of-buet-on-tuesday}} Since then, convocations have been held in 1976, 1992, 1993, 1997, 2001, 2004, 2005, 2006, 2011 and 2019.{{cite web |title=11th Convocation 2019|url=http://www.buet.ac.bd/home/Convocation|url-status=live|website=BUET|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190206224515/http://www.buet.ac.bd/home/Convocation|archive-date=6 February 2019}} ==Administration== [[File:Registrar Building BUET 1.A.M.R.jpg|right|thumb|Registrar Building established in 1930]] [[File:Old Academic Building BUET 1.A.M.R.jpg|right|thumb|Old Academic Building]] The [[Chancellor (education)#Bangladesh|Chancellor]] is the ceremonial head of the university who appoints the [[Chancellor (education)#Bangladesh 2|Vice-chancellor]]. The position is held by the incumbent [[President of Bangladesh]].{{Cite news |date=25 June 2020|title=Buet gets new VC, DU new Pro VC|url=https://www.thedailystar.net/buet-gets-new-vc-dhaka-university-new-pro-vc-1920421|access-date=9 April 2021|work=The Daily Star|language=en}}{{cite web |url=http://www.buet.ac.bd/?page_id=3|title=Administration|website=BUET|access-date=24 June 2016}} The Vice-chancellor is the executive head of the university. The position is always held by a senior Professor of the university. The university is administered by the University Syndicate which is chaired by the Vice-chancellor.{{Cite news |last=Quader|first=AKMA|title=Resurrection of BUET|url=https://en.prothomalo.com/opinion/Resurrection-of-BUET|access-date=9 April 2021|work=Prothom Alo|type=opinion|language=en}} Members of the Syndicate include Deans of several faculties, Director General of Secondary and Higher Education in Bangladesh, Director General of Technical Education in Bangladesh, eminent academics from this university as well as from other famous public universities. Each of the faculties is headed by a [[Dean (education)|Dean]] and each of the departments is chaired by a Head of the department. They are generally full professors from their respective faculties and departments. Institutes, Research Centers and Directorates are headed by the Directors who are full professors from relevant fields of research. Other major administrative posts include the [[Registrar (education)|Registrar]], the Comptroller and the Controller of Exams. The university has also the following Statutory Authorities. * Academic Council * Finance Committee * Faculties * Selection Boards * Committee for Advanced Studies and Research (CASR) * Planning and Development Committee * Boards of Postgraduate Studies (BPGS) * Boards of Undergraduate Studies (BUGS) The University Syndicate is the supreme authority in major policy-making matters and in approving recommendations. The Finance Committee, the Planning and Development Committee and other committees assist the Syndicate in matters important for the proper functioning of the university. The Academic Council is the supreme body for formulating academic rules and regulations to which the CASR, Boards of Undergraduate and Postgraduate Studies and the Faculties recommend. == List of vice-chancellors == Following is the complete list of the vice-chancellors.{{cite web |url=http://www.buet.ac.bd/Administration/PreviousVc|title=Previous Vice-chancellors|website=BUET|access-date=2 September 2017|archive-date=3 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170903031333/http://www.buet.ac.bd/Administration/PreviousVc|url-status=dead}} # [[M. Alee Murtuza]] (30 August 2002 – 29 August 2006) # [[A. M. M. Safiullah]] (30 August 2006 – 29 August 2010) # [[S M Nazrul Islam]] (30 August 2010 – 13 September 2014) # [[Khaleda Ekram]] (14 September 2014 – 24 May 2016) # [[Saiful Islam (academic)|Saiful Islam]] (22 June 2016 – 25 June 2020) # [[Satya Prasad Majumder]] (25 June 2020 – present) ==Admission== === Undergraduate === [[File:ECE Building, BUET.jpg|thumb|220 px|Electrical and Computer Engineering]] The undergraduate admission of BUET is based on grades and examinations. Extracurriculars or financial needs are not considered in the admission process.{{Cite web |title=Prospectus(26-02-2023).pdf |url=https://drive.google.com/file/d/16bV2FW_Q2pk_ai_A8PSNwuHGTeQLCf6a/view?usp=embed_facebook |access-date=2023-04-18 |website=Google Docs}} The undergraduate admission test is one of the most intensive written examinations in Bangladesh. After completion of [[Higher Secondary School Certificate|higher secondary level]] (HSC) education, a student can submit her or his application for undergraduate admission if he/she fulfills the minimum requirements. The students with the best grades in Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, English, and Bengali on their Higher Secondary School Certificate (HSC) examination are allowed to take the admission test. The screening process allows 20,000 students to sit for the admission test based on the cumulative sum of their GPA in those five subjects.{{Cite news |date=14 October 2019|script-title=bn:বুয়েটে ২০১৯-২০ শিক্ষাবর্ষের ভর্তি পরীক্ষা অনুষ্ঠিত|url=https://bangla.dhakatribune.com/bangladesh/2019/10/14/15889/%E0%A6%AC%E0%A7%81%E0%A7%9F%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%9F%E0%A7%87-%E0%A6%AD%E0%A6%B0%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%A4%E0%A6%BF-%E0%A6%AA%E0%A6%B0%E0%A7%80%E0%A6%95%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%B7%E0%A6%BE-%E0%A6%B6%E0%A7%81%E0%A6%B0%E0%A7%81|access-date=8 April 2021|work=Dhaka Tribune|language=bn}}{{cite web |url=http://ugadmission.buet.ac.bd/|title=Undergraduate Admission|website=BUET|access-date=3 October 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111011124127/http://ugadmission.buet.ac.bd/|archive-date=11 October 2011}} After the competitive admission test, about 1,275 students get selected on the basis of merit and are offered admission.{{Cite news |script-title=bn:বুয়েটে ভর্তিতে আবেদন শুরু, ১২১৫ আসনের জন্য পরীক্ষা দুই ধাপে|url=https://www.prothomalo.com/education/admission/বুয়েটে-ভর্তিতে-আবেদন-শুরু-১২১৫-আসনের-জন্য-পরীক্ষা-দুই-ধাপে|access-date=12 June 2021|work=Prothom Alo|language=bn}} The admission test is of 600 marks, with 60 questions carrying 10 marks each. 20 questions are from physics, 20 from chemistry and 20 from mathematics. There are 26 seats for foreign students at the undergraduate level.{{cite web |url=http://www.buet.ac.bd/wp-content/uploads/2015/08/UG_Foreign_2015-16.pdf|title=Foreign 2015-16|website=BUET|access-date=16 December 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160115173922/http://www.buet.ac.bd/wp-content/uploads/2015/08/UG_Foreign_2015-16.pdf|archive-date=15 January 2016|url-status=dead}} The pre-requisite qualification for admission is HSC or GCE [[A-level]] or its equivalent with high grades in Mathematics, Physics, and Chemistry. The admission fee is $200; the course registration fee is US$50 per [[Course credit|credit hour]] and the approximate cost of food, lodging etc. is US$100 per month. A maximum of 10 students from a single country are allowed for admission.{{Cite web |title=Prospectus for foreign students(27-2-2023).pdf |url=https://drive.google.com/file/d/1cV19o1JWz1XM628he90cuPj-5HBEx9EE/view?usp=embed_facebook |access-date=2023-04-18 |website=Google Docs}}[[File:Playground of BUET.jpg|right|thumb|Playground of BUET]] ===Postgraduate=== In [[Master's degree|Masters]] and [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] programs, around 1,000 graduate students are accepted on an annual basis. For admission to these programs, candidates are required to appear in [[interview]]s and/or written tests. Postgraduate degrees offered by departments and institutes are MSc (Master of Science), MSc Engg. ([[Master of Science in Engineering]]), M. Engg ([[Master of Engineering]]), MURP ([[Master of Urban and Regional Planning]]), MArch ([[Master of Architecture]]), M.Phil. ([[Master of Philosophy]]) and PhD ([[Doctor of Philosophy]]). [[Postgraduate diploma]]s (PG. Dip.) are also offered in [[Information technology|IT]] and [[Water resource management|Water resources development]]. ==Research programs== For consultation and research the expertise at the university, its teachers and the laboratory facilities are available to other organizations of the country. A separate institution – Bureau of Research, Testing and Consultation (BRTC) has been formed to oversee these activities.{{Cite news |last=|first=|script-title=bn:বুয়েটের গবেষণা সংস্থা পরামর্শক|url=https://www.prothomalo.com/business/%E0%A6%AC%E0%A7%81%E0%A7%9F%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%9F%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%B0-%E0%A6%97%E0%A6%AC%E0%A7%87%E0%A6%B7%E0%A6%A3%E0%A6%BE-%E0%A6%B8%E0%A6%82%E0%A6%B8%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%A5%E0%A6%BE-%E0%A6%AA%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%AE%E0%A6%B0%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%B6%E0%A6%95|access-date=8 Development Bank]], [[Department for International Development|DfID]], [[Japan International Cooperation Agency|JICA]] etc. In the wake of the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], BUET developed OxyJet, a
